rows.domain: for all deterministic realizations and pairs of admitted histories under one protected continuation obligation
rows.counterexample: If the two histories require the same continuation, merging them creates no contradiction.

rows.domain: for every predictive class p in finite exact target state S_O, with lossless fixed-length residual R
rows.counterexample: If reconstruction may be lossy, fewer residual symbols can be used.

rows.domain: for every universal simulator U, simulated target M, and integer delay d>0 under charged execution
rows.counterexample: If inserted no-ops are uncharged, the resource separation disappears.

rows.domain: for all bases B1,B2 and compiler-bound classes K closed under identity and composition
rows.counterexample: Without composition closure, two bounded compilers need not compose within K, so transitivity can fail.

rows.domain: for all H>=0, frozen nonnegative price vectors w, build burden K and per-use saving Delta
rows.counterexample: When Delta<=0, no positive reuse horizon makes retention cheaper.

rows.domain: for finite morphology set M and jointly distributed world W and pre-choice information Z with integrable frozen loss
rows.counterexample: If Z is observed after the choice, conditional selection cannot use it and the inequality need not be operationally attainable.

rows.domain: for all adapted proposal sequences with conditional target-hit probability at least p_min>0 before first hit
rows.counterexample: At p_min=0 a reachable process may avoid the target forever, so the geometric tail bound is unavailable.

rows.domain: for every fixed learning/update law over unrestricted appropriately closed problem classes
rows.counterexample: On a restricted smooth convex class, a declared descent law can dominate specified alternatives.

rows.domain: for finite K equipotent world classes requiring pairwise incompatible exact actions and lossless deterministic state
rows.counterexample: If two classes admit the same correct action, they need not occupy distinct state values.

rows.domain: for all four-cost tuples C0,CA,CB,CAB under the declared saved-cost interaction definition
rows.counterexample: A structural constraint fixing CAB=CA+CB-C0 fixes the interaction to zero.

rows.domain: for integers h>=0 with switch cost K>0 and constant future-block saving Delta>0
rows.counterexample: At K=0 switching is immediately weakly beneficial and migration-cost hysteresis vanishes.

rows.domain: for iid proposals from kernel Q(.|x), exact verifier, useful set U, and constant charged attempt cost c
rows.counterexample: With dependent proposals, first-hit burden need not equal c divided by one-step useful mass.

rows.domain: for all machines at fixed scope Omega and compiler class K closed under composition
rows.counterexample: Without composition closure, mutual bounded simulation need not define a transitive species equivalence.

rows.domain: for finite grammars, finite worlds, finite resource caps and decidable protected equivalence; contrasted with unrestricted programs
rows.counterexample: Removing any finiteness/decidability premise can make enumeration nonterminating or semantic equivalence undecidable.

rows.domain: for every proposed domain residual against the frozen D1-D8 parent set and eight admission gates
rows.counterexample: Omitting strongest-parent refusal permits an implementation variant to be mislabeled as a new domain.

rows.domain: for every claimed prospective outcome Y and prediction artifact P under an auditable custody order
rows.counterexample: If P can be edited after access to Y, agreement is compatible with post-hoc fitting.

rows.domain: for all admitted causal states theta with observation map O and protected target map I
rows.counterexample: Two states in one O-fiber with different I values make the factor g ill-defined.

rows.domain: for every finite intervention policy and every positive-probability terminal transcript cell
rows.counterexample: A transcript cell crossing two I-equivalence classes cannot support exact identification.

rows.domain: for all substrate states s under measurement map psi and protected cross-substrate target T
rows.counterexample: If T is constant on every psi-fiber, the stated identifiability obstruction disappears.

rows.domain: for iid bounded observations Xi in [0,1], fixed sample size N and fixed pre-data query
rows.counterexample: Outcome-adaptive repeated queries violate the fixed-query premise and need a sequential/adaptive guarantee.

rows.domain: for every finite set of distinct observed inputs and unrestricted function class containing polynomial perturbations
rows.counterexample: Restricting the hypothesis class to polynomials of degree below the sample count can restore uniqueness.

rows.domain: for every run whose events form a disjoint exhaustive lifecycle partition and every resource coordinate k
rows.counterexample: Overlapping stages double-count an event; a non-exhaustive partition undercounts.

rows.domain: for every theorem-shaped claim in the registered corpus and evidence rung P1-P5
rows.counterexample: A finite witness program alone does not establish its surrounding universal statement.

rows.domain: for every closure rung r, scope Omega and finite required gate set Gates(r)
rows.counterexample: One false required conjunct makes the closure conjunction false despite all other gates.

rows.domain: for every external-memory policy with absorption cost, per-use saving, invalidation hazard and finite horizon under frozen prices
rows.counterexample: Immediate invalidation or nonpositive per-use saving removes the absorption advantage.

rows.domain: for every typed learning object (state, update, feedback, loss, resources) and admitted specialization map
rows.counterexample: Without a common typed update object, two named learners need not be comparable specializations.

rows.domain: for finite developmental graphs, local move relations, target sets and bijective relabelings
rows.counterexample: Adding a nonlocal jump edge can remove a barrier proved only for the local move relation.

rows.domain: for finite solver menus with declared routing, verifier, fallback and lifecycle costs
rows.counterexample: An unsound verifier can accept an incorrect routed result, defeating semantic preservation.

rows.domain: for all finite capability mechanisms and registered joint/interventional capability functions
rows.counterexample: Marginal capability scores alone admit joint laws with opposite interaction signs.

rows.domain: for every predictor using descriptor X to identify target Y on the admitted finite scope
rows.counterexample: If Y is constant on X-fibers, a predictor exists and abstention is unnecessary.

rows.domain: for finite machine populations with typed variation, inheritance, interaction, reproduction and resource accounting
rows.counterexample: Without reproduction or persistence, invasion fitness and species abundance are undefined.

rows.domain: for deterministic time-homogeneous systems with finite joint inherited/developmental state
rows.counterexample: Unbounded state growth or an external nonperiodic clock removes the finite eventual-periodicity conclusion.

rows.domain: for registered dependent experiments under one global good event or dependence-safe union bounds
rows.counterexample: Multiplying marginal confidence levels without independence can overstate joint coverage.

rows.domain: for finite candidate sets with smooth burden laws, hard feasibility constraints and frozen price/resource axes
rows.counterexample: A discontinuous underlying burden law can create a physical transition, not merely an argmin crossover.

rows.domain: for finite sequence obligations, fixed/local/adaptive access policies and charged read budgets
rows.counterexample: If the target address is fixed, adaptive routing pays for a choice it never uses.

rows.domain: for finite symbolic transductions factored into selector state and emitter map
rows.counterexample: If selector fibers merge inputs requiring different outputs, no emitter can repair the lost distinction.

rows.domain: for finite program corpora, retained chunks, recurrence counts and charged discovery/storage/serve costs
rows.counterexample: At one use, retention overhead can exceed every saved primitive step.

rows.domain: for finite candidate sets with exact objective J and bias-optimal exhaustive or probability-weighted program search
rows.counterexample: If target proposal mass is zero, no finite hitting-time guarantee follows despite expressibility elsewhere.

rows.domain: for declared generative models whose inference/control objective exactly matches the control problem and resource accounting
rows.counterexample: Model misspecification or a mismatched preference objective breaks the control-as-inference equivalence.

p3_assumptions.T602-12: iid proposals, exact verifier, constant per-attempt cost, positive fixed useful-set mass
p3_assumptions.T602-19: iid Xi in [0,1], fixed N, fixed pre-data query and mean
p3_assumptions.T602-32: no hidden independence; one global good event or union-bound allocation over declared dependent stages

p4_experiments.T602-18: G10 held-out operational cross-substrate bridge protocol specified in the owning theorem section; positive bridge remains open

p5_consequences.T602-08: no universally best update law on unrestricted closed problem classes
p5_consequences.T602-10: no universal interaction sign without a structural joint-cost law
p5_consequences.T602-14: DOMAIN_BASIS_COMPLETE only at registered finite scope; universal absence certification forbidden
p5_consequences.T602-20: finite fit cannot license unrestricted extrapolation
p5_consequences.T602-31: finite time-homogeneous inherited state cannot establish unbounded open-ended evolution
p5_consequences.T602-33: finite selector changes are morphology crossovers, not thermodynamic phase transitions

NFL.consequence: unrestricted universal learner/morphology dominance is forbidden

RICE_HALTING.consequence: unrestricted extensional classification, semantic equivalence and total search guarantees are forbidden

GODEL.consequence: no sufficiently strong consistent formal system is treated as proving every truth in its own effective language

BLUM_SPEEDUP.consequence: no unrestricted problem class is assigned a final universally fastest realization

FINITE_STATE_OEE.consequence: finite time-homogeneous state has bounded distinguishability and eventual periodicity
